title: Grateful Dead Live at Star Theatre on 1970-03-08
lineage: SBD > MR > Cass > DAT > CD > SHN

ai_review.summary: Good soundboard capture of a chaotic Phoenix 1970 show – the acoustic Black Peter and Lovelight shine while an on‑stage guest both amuses and annoys.
ai_review.review: The recording is a generally clear soundboard source with occasional volume swings, making it very listenable. Musically the band delivers strong playing—Jerry’s sweet vocal on Black Peter and a superb acoustic set are highlights—but the surprise appearance of an uninvited vocalist/harmonica player disrupts several numbers (Not Fade Away, Impromptu Blues) and divides opinion. Overall the performance is energetic and memorable despite the guest’s antics.

ai_rating.rationale: Show quality is solid with standout acoustic moments, but the disruptive guest lowers enjoyment; recording quality is good overall, leading to a balanced 4‑star rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Pretty good sound quality with some volume fluctuations and occasional midside imbalance, but generally clear and very listenable.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The set features a strong acoustic segment (Pigpen’s solo, Black Peter) and an extended Not Fade Away → Lovelight transition that many reviewers cite as a high point. The unexpected guest singer/harmonica player interrupts several numbers, creating a chaotic but oddly entertaining atmosphere.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Vocals described as sweet, musical and ‘heart‑breakingly passionate’ on Black Peter; guitar work praised in acoustic sections.
band_member_comments.Bob: Voice noted as crystal clear and strong throughout the show.
band_member_comments.Drums: Drums described as tight and solid.
